lead.zh-Hans: 苏州的第一张速写，先从一个扇形开始。
lead.en: My first Suzhou sketch began with the shape of a fan.

text.zh-Hans: 拙政园水边的与谁同坐轩是扇形的，我把轮廓画在纸角。想连水里的倒影一起画，纸就显得太小了。我往左挪，邮包往右歪，像也想替我找角度。先留一半空白，明天把纸翻过来再试。
text.en: The pavilion beside the water in the Humble Administrator’s Garden has a fan-shaped outline. I fitted it into a corner of my paper, but there was no room for the reflection. I shifted left; the mailbag leaned right, offering an opinion. I saved some blank space. Tomorrow I will try the other side.

text.zh-Hans: 问问旁边的人喜欢哪个角度
text.en: Ask a nearby visitor for a favorite angle

text.zh-Hans: 翻过纸再画一次
text.en: Turn the sheet over and try again

lead.zh-Hans: 今天在苏州，我和另一位游客一起找路。
lead.en: Today in Suzhou, two visitors tried to give directions.

text.zh-Hans: 苏州博物馆的庭院里有池塘、假山和小桥。我和另一位游客互相问路，最后发现彼此指的是同一座小桥。我在余纸上画桥，他添上两个找路的我们，又把画留给我。桥倒画得很清楚，明天还得给我们补上朝向。
text.en: Suzhou Museum brings a pond, rockwork and bridges into its courtyard. Another visitor and I exchanged directions before realizing we meant the same bridge. I drew it on spare paper; they added two puzzled travelers and let me keep the sketch. The bridge is clear enough. Tomorrow our little figures need arrows.

text.zh-Hans: 把两个人的问路故事讲一遍
text.en: Retell the two-way directions

text.zh-Hans: 看看纸上的人朝着哪里
text.en: Check which way the drawn travelers face

lead.zh-Hans: 苏州今天寄来一碗纸上的面。
lead.en: A paper bowl of Suzhou noodles is enclosed today.

text.zh-Hans: 今天吃了苏式汤面，碗里有面、有汤，也有浇头。我画菜单时先画碗，再让一根面条绕着纸走，没想到绕得比碗还大。另拿一张纸试画，它又在边上打了结。小菜单和这团线都收好了，明天想试试从碗外画进去。
text.en: Today I had Suzhou soup noodles: noodles, broth and a topping sharing one bowl. On my menu, a single drawn noodle promptly grew larger than the bowl. A second attempt tied itself into a knot at the edge. I kept both. Tomorrow I might start outside the bowl and work inward.

text.zh-Hans: 请人猜猜这团线是什么
text.en: Ask someone to identify the tangled line

text.zh-Hans: 找找哪一圈绕出了碗
text.en: Find the loop that escaped the bowl

lead.zh-Hans: 今天的菜名，让铅笔先跑偏了一会儿。
lead.en: The name of lunch led my pencil briefly astray.

text.zh-Hans: 今天吃到松鼠鳜鱼，鱼做成松鼠似的形状，浇着酸甜的汁。我画手绘菜单时，一不留神给它添了两只耳朵。赶紧另画一遍，把想象出来的耳朵留给纸边的小邮包。菜单这一张总算画对了，明天再想想邮包该怎么戴帽子。
text.en: Lunch was squirrel-shaped mandarin fish with a sweet-and-sour sauce. Halfway through drawing the menu, I caught myself adding two squirrel ears. A fresh attempt sorted that out; the imaginary ears went onto a little mailbag in the margin. The menu is ready. Tomorrow comes the problem of fitting a hat over those ears.

text.zh-Hans: 给有耳朵的邮包起个名字
text.en: Find a name for the mailbag with ears

text.zh-Hans: 看看两张鱼图哪里不同
text.en: Compare the two fish drawings

lead.zh-Hans: 今天在苏州，菜单旁边也留出了说话的位置。
lead.en: Today in Suzhou, the menus left room for a conversation.

text.zh-Hans: 我今天尝了小份苏式汤面，也尝了松鼠鳜鱼。画好两张菜单后，一位邻座问哪张是面，我指着那团绕来绕去的线。他替我在纸角画了个小碗，我则把鱼图递过去给他猜。两张菜单都收好了，明天再问问他看出了什么。
text.en: Today I tried small portions of Suzhou soup noodles and squirrel-shaped mandarin fish. A neighbor looked at my two drawn menus and asked which was the noodles. I pointed to the tangled line. They added a little bowl in the corner, so I handed over the fish drawing for another guess. Both menus are ready; tomorrow I will ask what they saw.

text.zh-Hans: 听听邻座怎样描述鱼图
text.en: Hear the neighbor describe the fish sketch

text.zh-Hans: 看看小碗添在哪里最合适
text.en: Find the right corner for the little bowl

lead.zh-Hans: 苏州今天的两张菜单，一个绕圈，一个翘尾。
lead.en: Today’s Suzhou menus have loops on one and a tail on the other.

text.zh-Hans: 今天试过小份苏式汤面和松鼠鳜鱼，我把它们各画在一张纸上。汤面那张先画碗，再留出浇头的位置；鱼那张画了松鼠似的轮廓，把酸甜的汁记在旁边。等收起菜单，才发现两张纸背面连着同一道铅笔印。明天试试把那道线接成一条路。
text.en: After small tastes of Suzhou soup noodles and squirrel-shaped mandarin fish, I gave each its own sheet. The noodle drawing left room for the topping; the fish got its squirrel-like outline and a note about the sweet-and-sour sauce. Turning the menus over revealed one pencil mark continuing across both backs. Tomorrow that line might become a road.

text.zh-Hans: 问问这条路可以通向哪里
text.en: Ask where the pencil road could lead

text.zh-Hans: 把背面那道线接起来
text.en: Join the line across the two backs

lead.zh-Hans: 你说“{reply}”，我照着把那张扇亭草稿翻了一面。
lead.en: I followed your note, “{reply}”, and turned over the pavilion sketch.

text.zh-Hans: 纸背空着，我又画了一次与谁同坐轩。旁边一位旅人也在画，便和我换着添了几笔，还各替对方画上一只小邮包。他说这张折纸让我带走，自己在另一张纸上继续。现在两面都有风景，明天要试试怎样折才不会把邮包压住。
text.en: The back was blank, ready for another view of the fan-shaped pavilion. A traveler sketching beside me traded a few pencil strokes, and we each added a little mailbag to the other drawing. They sent me off with the folded sheet and started another. Both sides now have a view. Tomorrow I need a fold that spares the bags.

text.zh-Hans: 把两面速写介绍给别人
text.en: Introduce both sides of the sketch

text.zh-Hans: 试试不压到邮包的折法
text.en: Find a fold that misses the little bags

learned.zh-Hans: 翻一面还能看见新角度
learned.en: Another side can hold another view.

lead.zh-Hans: 苏州的扇形小轩，我想给你留个位置。
lead.en: Wishing you a seat in Suzhou’s fan-shaped pavilion.

text.zh-Hans: 与谁同坐轩的名字，让我在回苏州后想了很久。到了拙政园西部的水边，看到扇形的小轩，门窗和石桌也有相似的形状，我便想象你坐在对面。我不用忙着讲解，你可以自己找找还有哪里像扇子。信写到这里，我真的往对面让了让。虽然你还没来，坐着的时候，心里已经没那么空了。
text.en: “With Whom Shall I Sit?” was the name I kept thinking about after reaching Suzhou again. By the water in the western part of the Humble Administrator’s Garden, I found the fan-shaped pavilion, with fan shapes in its openings and stone table too. I imagined you opposite me, finding the shapes for yourself while I kept quiet. Writing this, I actually shifted to give you room. I rather like having company in mind.

text.zh-Hans: 聊聊想坐在什么位置
text.en: Talk about where you would sit

text.zh-Hans: 找找藏在门窗里的扇形
text.en: Find the fan shapes in the openings
